notes: The competing reading would make *forgiveness* the predicate and give it *there is*, leaving עִם a bare *with*; rule 49's closing paragraph decides for the prepositional predicate, since the clause's only nominal is the English subject of that copula and the presentative *there* is not a separate English subject but part of the construction-supplied frame under rule 20.
The Hebrew order כִּי־עִמְּךָ הַסְּלִיחָה (fronted prepositional phrase, definite nominal) was read for which side is the predicate rather than the ASV's word order, as rules 20 and 49 both direct.
